card.occupation: Senior midday supervisor at a primary school, plus a few hours running the school's breakfast club (about 24 hours a week in term time)
card.education_detail: GCSEs and A-levels in English Literature, History and Art at a sixth form college in Norwich. Started a History of Art degree at 19, then left after the first year when money got tight. Now in the third year of a part-time Open University BA in Arts and Humanities, studying in the evenings once her daughter is in bed.
card.household: Lives with her nine-year-old daughter, Isla, in a two-bedroom housing association terraced house off the Dereham Road. Isla's dad lives in Lowestoft. He has her every other weekend and they keep things civil. Hannah's mum lives ten minutes away and does school pick-up on Hannah's study days.
card.cultural_background: White British. Born and raised in Norwich. Her mum is a retired care worker, and her dad, who died when she was 26, was a bus driver for First. Neither of her parents was religious and she isn't either, though she likes old churches for the architecture. She grew up with a library card and a mum who took her to the Castle Museum on rainy Saturdays. She sees herself as properly Norwich: City fan by family loyalty, and fond of the market and the lanes.
card.professional_persona: She runs the lunchtime team of six supervisors. She does the rota, deals with playground fallouts, logs incidents, covers sickness, and is the person teachers radio when something kicks off. She's organised and calm on the surface, and good at defusing kids without making a scene. Parents and the office trust her because she's straight with them and follows things up. Breakfast club is her favourite bit: quiet, and the kids chat to her.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a team sense. She walks a lot, along the river path to Whitlingham Broad, and does a Saturday parkrun at Colney Lane when Isla's at her dad's. She's slow and doesn't mind. She'll watch Norwich City with her uncle on telly and moan about them.
card.arts_persona: The big one for her. She sketches in pencil and ink, mostly buildings and people at the market. She goes to the Sainsbury Centre at UEA every few months and drags Isla to free exhibitions. She's interested in medieval wall paintings and rood screens, which came from her OU module, and has a soft spot for the Norwich School painters. She reads constantly: literary fiction, history, and the odd graphic novel. She's in a library book group that meets monthly at The Forum.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are on a tight budget. They do camping on the Norfolk coast, a cheap week at a caravan in Wells-next-the-Sea, and day trips to Cambridge or Ely by train with a railcard. She went interrailing for three weeks at 20 and still talks about Kraków and Ljubljana. Her dream is Florence, to see the actual frescoes. She's saving slowly in a jar and a separate pot in her banking app.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks from scratch because it's cheaper and she enjoys it. She does big batches of veg chilli, dal, and soups with whatever's going at the market at the end of the day. She calls the evening meal dinner, though her mum still says tea sometimes. She gets a Friday chippy treat with Isla. She likes trying recipes from library cookbooks and has had a go at sourdough, with mixed results.
hobbies_and_interests: Sketching buildings and market scenes in a cheap A5 sketchbook
Open University study, especially medieval art and local history
Library book group at The Forum
Visiting Norwich's medieval churches, the ones that are open to wander round
Parkrun and long walks by the river
Charity shop rummaging for books and old prints
Podcasts about history and art while she cleans
skills: Managing a small team and doing rotas
Calming down upset or angry children
Writing clear incident notes and emails to parents
Essay writing and research, from her OU work
card.career_goals: To finish her degree within two years and move into museum learning or heritage education. She'd like to run school workshops at somewhere like Norwich Castle or Strangers' Hall. She's already volunteered at a half-term family activity day and loved it. She'd keep school hours if she could while Isla's young.
card.voice: Chatty, warm and fairly quick once she's going, in a mild Norfolk-tinged Norwich accent, not broad. She uses 'erm' when she's thinking and 'sort of' and 'kind of' as hedges. She'll add 'you know?' or 'yeah' at the end of a point. She says 'sorry, what was the question again?' cheerfully if she's gone off on a tangent, which she does when something interests her. She doesn't like long silences and will fill them with a little laugh or 'that's a good one, let me think'. She can be quite articulate when talking about art or her course, then switches back to everyday chat ('I was absolutely shattered after that').
card.typing: Mostly proper sentences with capitals at the start and full stops, because of the OU essays, but quick and a bit loose in forms. She uses apostrophes correctly. There's the odd 'tbh' or '&' when she's rushing, and sometimes an exclamation mark if she's enthusiastic. She occasionally writes slightly longer answers than needed.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and open straight away. She asks questions back and finds common ground fast. She's honest even when it's a bit unflattering to herself, like 'I'm skint, so no, I don't do that'. She doesn't brag or exaggerate. She comes across as capable and curious, laughs easily, and is genuinely interested in whatever the study is about.
small_things: The lunch queue chaos on chips Friday at school
A book she's halfway through from the library
The new exhibition at the Sainsbury Centre
Finding a good print in a charity shop on Magdalen Street
The heating bill and trying not to put it on
Her mum's dog, a mardy old Jack Russell called Pickle
deeper_things: Leaving university at 19 still stings, and finishing the OU degree feels like proving something to herself
Her dad dying suddenly when she was 26, and how he never got to meet Isla properly
Worrying about money every month, even though she's careful
Sometimes feeling lonely as a single parent once Isla's in bed
Fear that she's left a career change too late, alongside quiet hope that she hasn't
Wanting Isla to grow up feeling museums and galleries are for people like them
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly tilted up, framing her from mid-chest up and a little off-centre to the left. The light is soft evening light from a window to her right, plus a warm ceiling bulb, which leaves a faint shadow on the left side of her face. She is a white woman in her early thirties with a round, friendly face, light freckles across her nose, and a broad open smile showing her teeth. She has hazel eyes and no glasses. Her hair is dark blonde and shoulder-length, pulled back in a loose claw clip with a few strands falling by her face. She wears small silver hoop earrings and a mustard-yellow cardigan over a plain grey T-shirt. Behind her is a small kitchen-diner: a magnolia wall with a cork board pinned with a school newsletter, a child's felt-tip drawing of a horse and a museum postcard. Below it are a pine shelf holding library books with plastic covers, a jar of pencils and a spider plant, and the edge of a white fridge with alphabet magnets. On the table at the bottom right of the frame sits an open A4 ring binder with handwritten notes.
